title: Diamonds in the rif: Alignment-free comparative genomics analysis reveals strain-transcendent Plasmodium falciparum antigens amidst extensive genetic diversity.
authors: Lawton, Jonathan G; Zhou, Albert E; Stucke, Emily M; Takala-Harrison, Shannon; Silva, Joana C; Travassos, Mark A
journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
one_liner_zh: 该文用k-mer比较和AlphaFold结构预测分析疟原虫RIFIN/STEVOR蛋白家族多样性，虽涉及蛋白结构预测但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: The repetitive interspersed family (rif) and subtelomeric variable open reading frames (stevor) are highly diverse multi-gene families in the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum. Embedded on the surface of infected erythrocytes, RIFIN and STEVOR proteins are involved in cytoadherence and immune evasion, but the extent of family-wide sequence diversity across strains has yet to be comprehensively investigated in light of improved resolution of the subtelomeric genome sequences. Using a k-mer frequency approach, we analyzed long-read genomic sequence data from 18 geographically diverse P. falciparum genome assemblies, including lab strains and clinical isolates. We hypothesized that k-mer sequence comparison can identify existing RIFIN and STEVOR subgroups, identify novel subgroups, and generate more robust and reliable estimates of family-wide sequence diversity. Full-length RIFIN and STEVOR proteins shared on average 49.5% and 61.1% amino acid k-mer similarity, respectively, which fell to 25.1% and 20% in the hypervariable regions alone. Despite this diversity, we identified 11 RIFINs and five STEVORs that were conserved across strains above expected thresholds. A subset of these strain-transcendent genes was similar and syntenic to genes in related Plasmodium species, suggesting an ancient origin. Additionally, in silico structural predictions from AlphaFold showed that three-dimensional structures of RIFIN receptor-binding regions were more conserved than their sequences suggested. Evolutionarily constrained RIFINs and STEVORs may have critical functions in parasite survival or pathogenesis. This study provides a framework for investigating diversity in highly variable multi-gene families and highlights the potential of strain-transcendent RIFIN and STEVOR proteins as vaccine candidates.
abstract_zh: 重复散布家族（rif）和亚端粒可变开放阅读框（stevor）是疟原虫恶性疟原虫中高度多样的多基因家族。RIFIN和STEVOR蛋白嵌入感染红细胞表面，参与细胞黏附及免疫逃逸，但鉴于亚端粒基因组序列分辨率的提高，跨菌株的家族-wide序列多样性程度尚未得到全面研究。利用k-mer频率方法，我们分析了来自18个地理多样性恶性疟原虫基因组组装的长读长基因组序列数据，包括实验室菌株和临床分离株。我们假设k-mer序列比较能够识别现有的RIFIN和STEVOR亚群，发现新亚群，并生成更稳健可靠的家族-wide序列多样性估计。全长RIFIN和STEVOR蛋白平均共享49.5%和61.1%的氨基酸k-mer相似性，而在高变区域单独比较时，这一比例降至25.1%和20%。尽管存在这种多样性，我们识别出11个RIFIN和5个STEVOR在菌株间保守性超过预期阈值。这些跨菌株基因中的一部分与相关疟原虫物种中的基因相似且同线性，表明其具有古老起源。此外，AlphaFold的计算机结构预测显示，RIFIN受体结合区的三维结构比其序列所暗示的更为保守。进化上受约束的RIFIN和STEVOR可能在寄生虫生存或发病机制中具有关键功能。本研究为调查高度可变多基因家族中的多样性提供了框架，并强调了跨菌株RIFIN和STEVOR蛋白作为疫苗候选者的潜力。
